newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Exiled Cambodian prince leaves HK after failed home bid.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Cambodian prince leaves HK after failed home bid.

text.p: Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh left Hong Kong on Thursday after an abortive attempt to fly home to contest charges that he plotted to kill Cambodian Co-Premier Hun Sen.
A Hong Kong government spokeswoman told Reuters that Sirivudh had left Hong Kong but she did not say how he had left the territory and declined to say where he was heading.
"I can confirm the latest situation is that the prince has left Hong Kong," Mary Leung, a spokeswoman from the government's Security Branch said in response to Reuters inquiries.
She declined to divulge his destination or how he had left, saying: "This is his personal business and we don't disclose such information."
A source close to the case earlier told Reuters Sirivudh might head for Beijing, having been barred by two airlines from flying to Phnom Penh.
The prince had a permit to stay in Hong Kong until Thursday, the source said. Leung declined to comment on how long the prince had been allowed to remain in Hong Kong.
